answer: Every agent must lock tokens in an inlet registry before its messages count toward votes; the registry issues one rate-limited credential per locked stake, and slashable deposits are forfeited if linked accounts coordinate to evade the cap. A trellis of signed referrals lets auditors trace repeated funding and control patterns across identities, while a crystal-clear challenge window allows disputed links to be reviewed before rewards settle. Sybils remain possible, but an attacker must tie up real capital in each identity, risk losing it, and pay the cost of making accounts look independent.
